name: chute_porch_bay1
_why: the 20 degree porch leg of the crossing chute, in the right-hand lane of bay 1. The porch is the one stretch where a splitter rib stands in the flow, so this line proves a lane is still open end to end. A blocked lane would leave the part watertight and single-bodied, which is exactly why no other check would notice.

name: chute_ramp_bay1
_why: the 40 degree leg, from the end of the porch out into hopper A's mouth: 105mm enclosed under tray B and under hopper B's ramp. If anything closes this, half the bays silently stop feeding.

name: chute_porch_bay5
_why: the same porch lane in the far bay

name: chute_ramp_bay5
_why: the same ramp leg in the bay the right-hand rail buttress intrudes into

name: outlet_trayA_bay1
_why: tray A's outlet: from inside the tray, under the wall that separates it from tray B, into the chute

name: outlet_trayB_bay5
_why: tray B's outlet: from inside the tray, under hopper B's front wall, into hopper B

name: rail_groove_front
_why: the front joining groove must be open from its floor out of the top of the side wall, or a neighbouring module's rail cannot be lowered in
